info.title: Bugaboo API
info.description: The API of Bugaboo. The browser app uses exactly this API. Every error is application/problem+json with a stable code and a message key.

get.summary:
The projects the person sees, a page at a time: the top of the tree, the projects inside one,
or the projects that a search finds. Needs no permission of its own: it lists what the person
may see, which is nothing for a person without a role.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: The fields each item holds, separated by commas. The answer schema names every field that can be asked for; when this is left out the route's own small default is used.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where the page starts: the `next_cursor` of the page before.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items a page holds at most (default 50, at most 100).

parameters.name: inside
parameters.description:
The projects directly inside this one. Without it (and without `search`) the list is the top
of the tree.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Words that name the projects to find anywhere in the tree, in their name or short name.

parameters.name: outside
parameters.description:
Leave out this project and everything inside it. Ignored for a project the person does not
see, or that does not exist.

parameters.name: movable
parameters.description:
Only the places this project may be moved into by the person: not itself, not inside
itself, not where it is now, and only where they may move projects. Ignored for a project
the person does not see, or that does not exist.

patch.summary:
Changes the name or the short name of a project. A short name that is changed leaves the old
one with the project, so its old addresses keep working. Needs the permission *Change the
project's name, short name and settings*; a short name also needs the right to make projects
where the project sits.

200.description: The project as it is now.

400.description: The request is not valid (request.invalid, auth.password_too_short, auth.password_breached, auth.invitation_invalid, auth.passkey_rejected).

409.description: Something stands in the way of the change: a name that is taken, a change somebody made first, or a rule about moving projects (name.taken, edit.version_changed, project.move_lifts_no_access, project.move_into_itself, project.too_deep, project.preview_changed).

retry-after.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

post.summary:
Moves a project, with everything in it, into another project or to the top level. It works
only with the `preview` of a preview that is still true: when the projects, who has which
role or the levels of the roles changed since, it answers `project.preview_changed`. A move
after which somebody could take away a *No access* that applies to them is refused. Needs the
permission *Move sub-projects into or out of the project* in the old and the new parent.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: The ID of the project that moves.

400.description: The request is not valid (request.invalid, auth.password_too_short, auth.password_breached, auth.invitation_invalid, auth.passkey_rejected).

409.description: Something stands in the way of the change: a name that is taken, a change somebody made first, or a rule about moving projects (name.taken, edit.version_changed, project.move_lifts_no_access, project.move_into_itself, project.too_deep, project.preview_changed).

retry-after.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

AcceptBody.description: Somebody who makes an account from an invitation.

secret.description: The secret from the invitation link (the part after the `#`).

AccessBody.description: Whether other accounts on this computer can open a part of the data folder.

AddPasskeyBody.description: A passkey the device made, with the name the person gives it.

credential.description: The answer of the device, as the browser gives it.

label.description: The name of the passkey, like "Work laptop".

AuthStatusBody.description: What the app needs to know before anybody signs in.

passkeys_available.description: Passkeys can be used: the public address of the server has a host name.

setup_needed.description: No administrator exists yet: the first-start setup with the setup code is open.

sign_up_open.description: People may sign up on their own.

codes.description: The codes. They are not stored in this form and cannot be shown again.

CertificateBody.description: The HTTPS certificate the server uses itself.

ChallengeBody.description: A challenge for a passkey, as the passkey library writes it.

challenge_id.description: Names the waiting challenge; hand it back with the answer.

options.description: What the device is asked, to give to `navigator.credentials`.

ChangeProjectBody.description: What to change about a project: what is left out stays as it is.

short_name.description: A new short name. The old one stays with the project.

version.description: The version the person looked at.

CodeAppBody.description: What the setup screen of the code app shows.

otpauth_url.description: The address the code app reads.

qr_png_base64.description: The QR picture of the address (PNG, base64).

secret.description: The secret as text, for typing it into the app.

CodeBody.description: The code of the second step.

code.description: A code from the code app (six digits) or a backup code.

ConfirmCodeBody.description: The first code of the code app, and the password typed again.

CreatedInvitationBody.description: A new invitation: the secret is shown only now.

link_path.description:
The page the link opens, with the secret after the `#`. Put the address of this server
in front. The secret is not stored and cannot be shown again.

DataFolderOpenBody.description:
Which parts of the data folder other accounts on this computer can open. Bugaboo only looks;
a folder that somebody made or moved keeps its rights.

database.description: The built-in database file and the files next to it.

setup_code_file.description: The file with the setup code of a server without a console.

kind.description: Which one it is. The address is never shown: it can hold a password.

ErrorCode.description: What went wrong. Clients react to this text, which never changes.

FieldLevelChangeBody.description: A level of a field that the move changes for the person.

InvitationBody.description: An invitation as the administrator sees it.

InvitationItem.description:
An invitation in a list: the fields that can be asked for. An answer holds only those that
were asked for.

InvitationLookupBody.description: Which address an invitation is for.

email.description: The address the account will get.

LiftBody.description: Somebody who could take away a *No access* that applies to them after the move.

person.description: The person, as the person who asks may see them.

project.description: The project the *No access* is on.

LogBreakBody.description: Why the chain of the security log does not verify.

LogResult.description: The result of checking the security log.

MeBody.description:
Who is signed in, and what they may do for the whole organization (the menus of the browser app
follow it; the server decides again at every request).

email.description: The e-mail address used to sign in.

permissions.description: What the person may do for the whole organization.

MoveBody.description: Where a project goes, and the version of the preview that was looked at.

preview.description: The `preview` of the answer to the preview that was looked at.

to.description: The ID of the project it goes into; `null` for the top level.

MovePreviewBody.description: What a move would do, before anything happens.

blocked.description: The move would be refused: somebody could take away a *No access* that applies to them.

blocked_out_of_sight.description: Something in a project the person cannot see also stops the move.

lifts.description: Who could take away a *No access* after the move and could not before.

people.description: Who gains or loses access or changes role, in the projects the person sees.

preview.description:
The version of this preview. The move asks for it, and works only while nothing it was made
from has changed.

oneOf.description: Where it would go, when the person may see that project; `null` for the top level.

truncated.description: The list was cut: it names the first people it found.

MoveRightBody.description: Where a person may move a project to.

short_name.description:
The letters of its issue IDs and address: 2 to 10 capital letters or digits, starting with a
letter.

Page_InvitationItem.description:
One page of a list. `T` is the view of an item for the API description; an answer holds the
items cut to the chosen fields ([`Page::of_authorized`]).

items.description:
An invitation in a list: the fields that can be asked for. An answer holds only those that
were asked for.

next_cursor.description: The cursor of the next page; `null` on the last page.

Page_ProjectItem.description:
One page of a list. `T` is the view of an item for the API description; an answer holds the
items cut to the chosen fields ([`Page::of_authorized`]).

items.description:
A project in a list: the fields that can be asked for. An answer holds only those that were
asked for.

has_sub_projects.description: Whether it holds sub-projects the person sees. A yes or no, never a number.

oneOf.description: The project it is inside, when the person may see that one.

short_name.description: The letters of its issue IDs and address.

next_cursor.description: The cursor of the next page; `null` on the last page.

PasskeyAnswerBody.description: What the device answered to a passkey challenge.

credential.description: The answer of the device, as the browser gives it.

id.description: The ID to remove it with.

label.description: The name the person gave it.

last_used_at.description: When it was last used to sign in.

PasswordBody.description: The new password with the current one.

PasswordOnlyBody.description: A password typed again before a sensitive change.

PeopleLevelChangeBody.description: A level of a kind of people information that the move changes for the person.

PersonBody.description: Who a person is, as the browser app shows them.

email.description: The e-mail address used to sign in.

PersonChangeBody.description: What a move changes for one person.

person.description: The person, as the person who asks may see them.

projects.description: The projects where something changes for them.

oneOf.description: By name, with the ID for links.
By the label of their role; the screen says "a {role}". No ID.
A removed person: the screen says "Former user {label}". No ID.

PersonRef.description: How a person is shown to one viewer.

Problem.description:
The body of an error answer, as plain data. The HTTP layer only sends it.

Clients react to `code` and show the message for `message_key` and `params` in their own
language. `title` is the English text, only a fallback for clients that cannot do that. The
fields are private and the only way to make a `Problem` is from an [`ErrorCode`], so no answer
carries a text or a status that does not belong to its code.

message_key.description: The key of the message to show, in the message catalog.

params.description: Values for the placeholders of the message. Empty today: error messages have none.

request_id.description: The ID of the request, also in the `x-request-id` header, to quote when asking for help.

title.description: The English text, a fallback for clients that cannot look up the message.

type.description: A stable address of the kind of error, `urn:bugaboo:error:<code>`.

ProjectBody.description: A project after it was made, changed or moved.

parent.description: The project it is inside, when the person may see that one.

short_name.description: The letters of its issue IDs and address.

version.description: Counts up with every change. A change is made on the version that was looked at.

ProjectChangeBody.description: What a move changes for one person in one project that moves.

after.description: What they would have after the move.

gains.description: What they could not do and could after the move.

loses.description: What they could do and could not after the move.

now.description: What the person has there now.

people.description: The kinds of people information whose level changes.

ProjectDetailBody.description: One project, with where it is and what the person may do there.

may_change_short_name.description: Whether the person may change the short name.

may_move.description: Where the person may move the project to.

permissions.description: What the person may do here.

project.description: The project. Its `short_name` is the one it has now, also when the address named an old one.

trail.description:
*Where you are*: the projects above it that the person sees, from the top down. It stops at
the first one they cannot see.

ProjectItem.description:
A project in a list: the fields that can be asked for. An answer holds only those that were
asked for.

has_sub_projects.description: Whether it holds sub-projects the person sees. A yes or no, never a number.

oneOf.description: The project it is inside, when the person may see that one.

short_name.description: The letters of its issue IDs and address.

ProjectRef.description: A project as a small reference: what a name in a sentence needs.

short_name.description: The letters of its issue IDs and address.

SecondStepBody.description: Which ways there are to finish signing in.

backup_code.description: A backup code (only with a code app).

code_app.description: A code from the code app.

SecretBody.description: The secret of an invitation link.

secret.description: The secret from the link (the part after the `#`).

SecurityLogBody.description: What checking the security log found.

anchored.description:
Whether the file that vouches for the end of the log exists. A log with entries and no
anchor is a warning: nothing then shows that the end was not cut off.

broken_at.description: The place of the first entry that does not verify (when it breaks).

entries.description: How many entries were checked (when it verifies).

head_hash.description: The start of the hash of the last entry, to compare with a copy kept elsewhere.

head_seq.description: The place of the last entry (when it verifies and has entries).

oneOf.description: What is wrong with it (when it breaks).

write_failures.description:
How many entries could not be written since the server started. A failed write does not
stop a sign-in, so a number above zero means the log lags: check the disk and the rights
on the data folder.

ServerStatus.description: What `GET /api/v1/status` answers: the server is up.

status.description: Always `ok`; an answer at all means the server is running.

ServerStatusBody.description: The status of the server, as the status page shows it.

oneOf.description:
The HTTPS certificate; missing when the server does not speak HTTPS itself (plain HTTP
behind a proxy) or the certificate cannot be read.

data_folder_open.description: What of the data folder other accounts on this computer can open.

security_log.description: The check of the security log.

uptime_seconds.description: How long it has been running, in seconds.

SessionBody.description: One session in *Where you're signed in*.

browser.description: The name of the browser, if known.

current.description: Whether this is the session of the request.

id.description: The ID to end it with.

last_seen_at.description: The last time it was used.

network.description: The network it came from, shortened.

system.description: The name of the system, if known.

sessions.description:
Newest first. A person has only a few, so the list is not paged: it has a hard cap, and
`truncated` says when the cap cut it off (M1-F44).

truncated.description: There are more sessions than the list holds.

SetupBody.description: The first administrator, with the setup code.

code.description: The setup code the server printed.

email.description: The e-mail address of the administrator.

SignInBody.description: What a person types to sign in.

SignUpBody.description: Somebody who makes an account on their own.

SignUpPolicyBody.description: Who may sign up on their own.

domains.description: The e-mail domains that may sign up. Empty: every domain, while signing up is on.

enabled.description: Whether signing up without an invitation is on.

SignedInBody.description: The answer to signing in. The cookies come with it.

oneOf.description:
Who signed in. Left out while the second step is still to do: a password alone shows
nothing about the person.

When present, the password was right but the person still has to finish with one of
these ways before anything else opens.

StandingBody.description: What a person has in one project.

held_back.description: A *No access* holds the person back there.

roles.description: The names of their roles there, in the order of roles.

StatusValue.description: The only value a status can have today.

TwoStepBody.description: How the second step of a person is set up.

backup_codes_left.description: How many backup codes are left.

code_app.description: Whether a code app is set up.

passkeys.description:
The passkeys. A person has at most 20, so the list is not paged: it has a hard cap, and
`truncated` says when the cap cut it off (M1-F44).

truncated.description: There are more passkeys than the list holds.

to.description: The ID of the project it would go into; `null` for the top level.

WordBody.description:
A word of the vocabulary with the message that names it: a field, a kind of people information
or a level.

code.description: The word, as it stands in the API (`cost-center`, `can-see`).

message_key.description: The key of the message that names it.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Signing in, sessions, second step, passkeys, invitations and setup.

tags.name: admin
tags.description: What only administrators see: the state of the server.
